guide.addLocation.step3: Upload a Store Photo (*) - required for new stores. Format: JPG/PNG, max 2MB. The map picker below helps you pinpoint the store location.
guide.addLocation.step4: Set Category (Main Branch/Branch/Warehouse/Office). Pick Manager from employee data - click the field to open employee list and select one.
guide.addLocation.step5: Configure Operating Hours (weekly), Social Media links, and toggle Active/Inactive status. Active stores can process transactions.
guide.addLocation.step6: Save via the 'Save Location' button or save as Draft. System validates required fields before submitting.
guide.addCategory.title: Add Category Guide
guide.addCategory.step1: Enter Category Name (*) - This is the main identifier that will appear in product lists, filters, and reports. Use clear, descriptive names like 'Beverages', 'Electronics', or 'Dairy Products'. This name is what you'll select later when adding products.
guide.addCategory.step2: Add Description (optional) - Provide details about what products belong in this category. This helps staff understand categorization and appears in detailed views. Example: 'All cold beverages including coffee-based and non-coffee drinks'.
guide.addCategory.step3: Select Icon or Upload Image - Choose from preset icons or upload a custom image. This visual identifier appears in category lists and helps with quick recognition at the cashier and product pages.
guide.addCategory.step4: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active categories can be assigned to products. Inactive categories are hidden from product forms but retain existing product assignments.
guide.addCategory.step5: After saving, this category will be available in the Add Product form under the Category dropdown. Go to Add Product to create products under this category. Categories are also visible in the cashier panel for filtering products by group.
guide.addSupplier.title: Add Supplier Guide
guide.addSupplier.step1: Enter Supplier Company Name (*) - This is the business entity that supplies your products. It will appear in purchase orders, stock reports, and supplier lists.
guide.addSupplier.step2: Enter Contact Person - The name of the person responsible at the supplier company. This person will be referenced in purchase orders and communication logs.
guide.addSupplier.step3: Complete Phone Number and Email - Contact details for placing orders, negotiating prices, or resolving delivery issues. These will be available in the supplier detail view.
guide.addSupplier.step4: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active suppliers are available for purchase orders. Inactive suppliers are preserved in history but cannot be used for new orders. Click Save to register the supplier in the system.
guide.addProduct.title: Add Product Guide
guide.addProduct.step1: Select Store (Super Admin only) - If you are Super Admin, choose one or more stores for this product. Each selected store will have this product listed. If NO store exists yet, click the 'Add Store' button to create one first. For non-Super Admin, the product is automatically added to your assigned store.
guide.addProduct.step2: Enter Product Name (*) & Basic Info - This is the product name that appears on receipts, sales reports, and inventory. Fill optional fields: Brand, Barcode, SKU, Unit (default pcs), Description. The barcode/SKU helps with tracking and quick scanning at the cashier.
guide.addProduct.step3: Select Category (*) & Supplier - Choose a Category from the dropdown. If no category exists yet, go to Category Management first to create one. Categories help organize products in the cashier panel and reports. Select Supplier and Tax (Super Admin only). These connect the product to its vendor for purchase orders.
guide.addProduct.step4: Set Pricing & Stock - Selling Price (*) is required. Cost Price helps track profitability. Stock quantity sets initial inventory. Min Stock triggers low-stock alerts. Points can be assigned for loyalty rewards. For batch tracking, enable 'Has Batch' to manage expiry dates and batch numbers.
guide.addProduct.step5: Variants & Modifiers - Enable 'Has Variant' for products with variations (e.g., size Small/Medium/Large, color Red/Blue). Each variant can have its own price and stock. Enable 'Has Modifier' for add-ons (e.g., extra cheese, topping). These appear in the cashier when the product is selected.
guide.addProduct.step6: Upload Product Image - Visual identification for the product (PNG, JPG, WEBP up to 2MB). Appears in the cashier product grid and customer receipts. Set Status (Active/Inactive) and Availability. Active products are available for sale.
guide.addProduct.step7: Save - Review all information. Click 'Next' through all 3 steps, then click 'Save' to save. You can also save as Draft to complete later. After saving, the product will be available in the cashier for checkout and tracked in inventory.
guide.addMember.title: Add Member Guide
guide.addMember.step1: Enter Full Name (*) - The customer's identity for the loyalty program. This appears on member cards, point transactions, and sales history.
guide.addMember.step2: Enter Phone Number (*) - Used for member lookup at checkout and communication. Members can be searched by phone number during sales.
guide.addMember.step3: Complete additional data: Birth Date, Gender, and Address. These enable birthday promotions and demographic analysis in reports.
guide.addMember.step4: Select Membership Tier - If NO tiers have been created yet, the dropdown will be empty. Go to Member Tier first to create tiers (e.g., Silver, Gold, Platinum). If tiers exist, select one to determine the member's benefits and discount level. Initial Points can be added as a welcome bonus. Click Save to register the member.
guide.addMemberTier.title: Add Member Tier Guide
guide.addMemberTier.step1: Set Tier Name (*) - Enter a unique name like 'Silver', 'Gold', or 'Platinum'. This is the level displayed on member profiles, cards, and receipts. Higher tiers should offer better benefits.
guide.addMemberTier.step2: Set Minimum Points (*) - The number of loyalty points required to reach this tier. Points are accumulated from customer purchases. Each tier must have a higher minimum than the previous level.
guide.addMemberTier.step3: Set Discount Percentage (*) - The discount amount members at this tier receive on purchases. Automatically applied at checkout for eligible products. Higher tiers typically get larger discounts.
guide.addMemberTier.step4: Visual Identity - Choose a badge Icon (Star, Premium, Medal, Diamond, Plus) and Color for this tier. The badge appears on member profiles, lists, and receipts for quick recognition.
guide.addMemberTier.step5: Benefits & Perks - List the advantages members get at this level (e.g., 'Free delivery', 'Priority service', 'Double points weekend'). These perks are shown on the member's profile.
guide.addMemberTier.step6: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active tiers are available for member assignments. Inactive tiers cannot be selected when creating/editing members but retain existing member data.
guide.addMemberTier.step7: Save & Chain to Members - Click Save to create the tier. After saving, go to Add Member to assign this tier to customers. Members will earn points and receive discounts based on their assigned tier.
guide.addStockOpname.title: Add Stock Opname Guide
guide.addStockOpname.step1: Set Audit Date (*) and Auditor Name (*) - Choose the audit date and enter the person responsible for the stock opname. This information identifies when and who performed the inventory check.
guide.addStockOpname.step2: Upload Excel or Download Template - Use the Download Template button to get a pre-formatted Excel file. Fill it with your inventory data offline. When you Upload Excel, the data is parsed and shown in the table first for review before saving. You can edit rows, fix data, and then save. For large inventories, this is faster than manual entry.
guide.addStockOpname.step3: Fill Item Rows - Each row represents one product. Enter Product Code, Product Name (*), Unit (e.g., pcs, kg), and Location. Click the search icon to find products from the existing product list. Use +Add Product to add more rows.
guide.addStockOpname.step4: Enter Stock Data - For each item, fill: Opening Stock, Incoming Items (since last check), Outgoing Items. The system calculates Ending Stock = Opening + Incoming - Outgoing.
guide.addStockOpname.step5: Enter Physical Stock & View Difference - Fill the Physical Stock column with the actual count from your physical inventory. The system automatically calculates the Difference (Physical - Ending Stock). Positive = surplus, Negative = shortage.
guide.addStockOpname.step6: Add Notes - Add per-item notes in each row explaining any discrepancies. Add overall audit notes in the text area at the bottom. Notes help explain stock differences during review.
guide.addStockOpname.step7: Save - Click 'Save & Complete' to finish the opname (automatically marked as Completed). Use 'Save as Draft' to save progress and finish later. The opname will appear in the Stock Opname list.
guide.addDepartment.title: Add Department Guide
guide.addDepartment.step1: Enter Department Name (*) - The name of the unit or division within your company (e.g., 'Kitchen', 'Finance', 'Marketing'). This department will be selectable when creating Positions.
guide.addDepartment.step2: Add Description (optional) - Describe the function, responsibilities, and scope of this department. Example: 'Handles all food preparation and kitchen operations.' This helps staff understand the department's role.
guide.addDepartment.step3: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active departments are available for position assignments. Inactive departments are hidden from position forms but retain existing position data.
guide.addDepartment.step4: Save - Click Save to create the department. After saving, go to Add Position to assign positions (e.g., 'Head Chef', 'Cashier Supervisor') under this department. Departments organize job roles in the company structure.
guide.addPosition.title: Add Position Guide
guide.addPosition.step1: Enter Position Name (*) - The job title or role name (e.g., 'Senior Cashier', 'Head Chef', 'Store Supervisor'). This position will be assigned to employees and appears on employee profiles and reports.
guide.addPosition.step2: Select Department (*) - Choose the department this position belongs to. This is MANDATORY. If NO departments exist yet, a message will appear with a button 'Add Department' to create one first. The department dropdown shows all active departments from the Department Management page. This links the position to its organizational unit for reporting and structure.
guide.addPosition.step3: Add Description (optional) - Describe the responsibilities, skills required, and scope of this position. Example: 'Responsible for managing daily cash register operations and customer payments.' This helps HR and managers understand the role.
guide.addPosition.step4: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active positions can be assigned to employees. Inactive positions are hidden from employee forms but retain existing employee assignments.
guide.addPosition.step5: Save - Click Save to create the position. After saving, go to Employee Management to assign this position to employees. Employees with this position will have their role and department information recorded in the system.
guide.addEmployee.title: Add Employee Guide
guide.addEmployee.step1: Fill Personal Information (*) - Enter Full Name, Username, Email, Password, Phone Number, Place of Birth, Address, Gender, and Date of Birth. The Employee ID is auto-generated. These details identify the employee and are used for login credentials.
guide.addEmployee.step2: Select Department & Position - Choose Department from existing departments (created in Department Management). Then select a Position that belongs to that department (created in Position Management). If no departments exist, create them first. This links the employee to their organizational role.
guide.addEmployee.step3: Select Store & Shift - Choose the Store/Location where the employee works. Then select their Shift (depends on the selected store - shifts must be created in Shift Management first). If no stores exist, create one in Store Management first.
guide.addEmployee.step4: Set Employment Type & Salary - Choose type: Full Time, Part Time, Contract, or Internship. For Contract/Internship, set Start Date and Duration - the End Date is auto-calculated. Enter Monthly Salary; the Daily Salary is auto-calculated for payroll.
guide.addEmployee.step5: Upload Photo & Documents - Upload a profile photo (JPG, PNG, max 2MB). Upload employee documents (PDF, DOC, XLS, JPG, PNG - multiple files). These files are stored and visible in the employee detail page.
guide.addEmployee.step6: Set Account & Status - Select Role (default: User) and optional Additional Access Menu for permissions. Toggle Active/Inactive status. Active employees can log in and access the system. Inactive employees retain data but cannot log in.
guide.addEmployee.step7: Save - Review all information. Click 'Save' to register the employee. Use 'Save as Draft' to complete later. After saving, the employee appears in Employee List and can be assigned to shifts, sales, and store operations.
guide.addTax.title: Add Tax Guide
guide.addTax.step1: Enter Tax Name (*) - The display name for this tax configuration (e.g., 'PPN 11%', 'PPh 0.5%'). This name appears when selecting tax in the Add Product form and on receipts.
guide.addTax.step2: Select Tax Type (*) - Choose from: PPN (Pajak Pertambahan Nilai / Value Added Tax), PPh (Pajak Penghasilan / Income Tax), or Non-Pajak (Non-Tax). Determines how the tax is calculated and reported.
guide.addTax.step3: Set Tax Rate (*) - The percentage rate for this tax (e.g., 11 for 11%, 0.5 for 0.5%). This rate is automatically applied to product prices when the tax is selected in the product form.
guide.addTax.step4: Add Description (optional) - Provide details about this tax, its regulations, or applicable products. Example: 'VAT 11% for all food and beverage products.'
guide.addTax.step5: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active taxes appear in the Add Product form for selection. Inactive taxes are hidden from selection but retain existing product assignments.
guide.addTax.step6: Save & Chain to Products - Click Save to create the tax. After saving, go to Add/Edit Product to apply this tax to products. The tax will be automatically calculated on the selling price at checkout and appear on receipts. Connected to sales reports for tax reporting.

guide.dashboard.s1desc: This tour will walk you through the header and dashboard, one by one. You can exit anytime using the close button.
guide.dashboard.s2desc: Quickly find any page or feature in the app. Click here or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K to open the command palette.
guide.dashboard.s3desc: Switch the interface language between Indonesian (ID) and English (EN). Your choice is saved for this session.
guide.dashboard.s4desc: Toggle between light and dark themes. The choice is applied instantly across the whole app.
guide.dashboard.s5desc: Click the LifeBuoy button in the header or the floating button at the bottom right to start the guide tour. The Support section in the sidebar opens the Help page.
guide.dashboard.s6desc: See real-time alerts for new orders, low stock, and system events. The red badge shows how many unread notifications you have.
guide.dashboard.s7desc: Access your profile settings or sign out of the system. Your role and username are shown here.
guide.dashboard.s8desc: Before this dashboard shows real data, complete the initial setup: add at least 1 store location, create products with categories, and (optionally) add members. This section displays 5 summary cards — Revenue (today's earnings + trend), Orders (total transactions), Active Products, Member count, and Low Stock (highlighted red when items need restocking). guide.dashboard.s10desc: List of the latest transactions. View status, totals, and order details, or print a receipt directly from here.

guide.location.s11bdesc: This card shows the total number of store locations registered in the system — both active and inactive combined.
guide.location.s11cdesc: Stores currently operational. The percentage below shows what portion of your total stores are active.
guide.location.s11ddesc: Stores marked as closed or paused. Click the card to filter the list down to only these stores.
guide.location.s11edesc: Number of unique cities where your stores operate. Useful for tracking your geographic reach.

guide.location.s11gdesc: All stores are listed here. Use the search bar above the table to filter by name or city. Each row has Detail, Edit, and Delete actions.
guide.category.s12adesc: Categories group your products (e.g. Food, Drinks, Snacks). Next we will walk through every element: the 3 summary cards, 4 header buttons, and the data table.
guide.category.s12bdesc: Total number of categories — both active and inactive combined.
guide.category.s12cdesc: Categories currently in use by your products. The percentage shows how many of your categories are active.
guide.category.s12ddesc: Categories that have been archived or have no products. Click the card to filter the list to inactive categories only.
guide.category.s12edesc: Downloads a blank Excel template with the correct column headers. Use this when you want to bulk-add categories via spreadsheet.
guide.category.s12fdesc: Exports the current list of categories (with images and product counts) as an Excel file for backup or reporting.

guide.supplier.s13adesc: Keep a list of all product suppliers. Next we will walk through every element: 3 summary cards, the Add button, the search bar, and the data table.
guide.supplier.s13bdesc: Total number of suppliers — active and inactive combined.
guide.supplier.s13cdesc: Suppliers you currently work with. The percentage shows the share of active suppliers.

guide.ingredient.s14cdesc: Count of ingredients with stock at or below minimum threshold. Plan reorders accordingly.

guide.position.s18ddesc: Positions that are no longer in use. Click the card to filter the list down to inactive positions only.

guide.addLocation.s1desc: Enter your store's basic details: store name, store ID (auto-generated), phone number, and email address. Ensure all fields marked with * are filled correctly.
guide.addLocation.s2desc: Fill in the full address: select province, city, district, and village from dropdowns. The postal code will be auto-filled based on your selection. You can also add additional location details in the 'Detail Location' field.
guide.addLocation.s3desc: Upload a clear photo of your store (JPG or PNG, max 2MB) to enhance visual recognition in the system. Click the upload area or drag & drop your image.
guide.addLocation.s4desc: Activate or deactivate your store using the toggle switch. Active stores can process transactions, while inactive stores are temporarily disabled.
guide.addLocation.s5desc: Review all entered information, then click the 'Save Location' button to save. The system will validate your data before storing it in the database.
guide.dailyReport.s25adesc: View daily business summary including total transactions, revenue, HPP, and profit. Filter by date range.
guide.cashflow.s25cdesc: Monitor cash inflows from sales (cash, QRIS, transfer) and outflows for financial management.
guide.shift.s26adesc: Manage work shifts. Create morning, afternoon, or night shifts. Shifts are assigned to employees and used in transaction reporting.
guide.shift.s26bdesc: Click the Add button to create a new shift. Fill in the shift name, type (daily/weekly), start & end time, date range, and assign employees.
guide.shift.s26cdesc: View all created shifts in the table. Each shift shows its schedule, assigned employees, and status. You can edit or delete shifts from here.
guide.sales.s28adesc: View detailed sales transactions history. Filter by date, store, payment method. Export data for accounting purposes.
guide.bestselling.s28bdesc: See which products sell the most. Analyze sales volume and revenue to identify top-performing items for inventory and marketing decisions.
guide.payment.s26bdesc: Manage payment methods available at checkout: Cash, QRIS, Bank Transfer. These appear in the cashier payment selection.
guide.addShift.title: Add Shift Guide
guide.addShift.step1: Enter Shift Name (*) - The name for this work shift (e.g., 'Shift Pagi', 'Shift Malam'). This appears in employee assignment and transaction reports.
guide.addShift.step2: Set Start Time (*) and End Time (*) - Define the working hours for this shift. Used to track which shift processed each transaction.
guide.addShift.step3: Add Description (optional) - Additional notes about this shift, such as team members or special instructions.
guide.addShift.step4: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active shifts are available for employee assignment and appear in shift selection.
guide.addShift.step5: Save & Chain to Employees - After saving, go to Employee Management to assign this shift to employees. Transactions will be grouped by shift for reporting.
guide.addTypePayment.title: Add Payment Method Guide
guide.addTypePayment.step1: Enter Payment Name (*) - The display name (e.g., 'Tunai', 'QRIS', 'Transfer Bank'). This appears in the cashier payment selection screen.
guide.addTypePayment.step2: Select Type (*) - Choose from: Tunai (cash), Non-Tunai (cashless), or Transfer. Determines how the payment is categorized in cash flow reports.
guide.addTypePayment.step3: Add Description (optional) - Details about this payment method, such as fees or processing time.
guide.addTypePayment.step4: Set Status (Active/Inactive) - Active methods appear in cashier checkout. Inactive methods are hidden from selection.
guide.addTypePayment.step5: Save & Chain to Transactions - After saving, this payment method will be available in the cashier checkout modal. All transactions using this method will be tracked in sales reports and cash flow.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.title: Create Purchase Order Guide
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step1: Select or add Supplier - Search for existing suppliers or type a new supplier name to add it directly.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step2: Select PIC (*) - Search and select the employee responsible for this purchase order.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step3: Set PO Date and Time (*) - Choose the order date and time.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step4: Add Items - Enter the name of the raw material/item to order, quantity, and unit price.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step5: Auto-calculated total - The system calculates the total based on qty x price for each item.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step6: Add Notes (optional) - Notes for the supplier or shipping information.
guide.addPurchaseOrder.step7: Save PO - Click Save PO to create the purchase order. Initial status: Pending.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.title: Edit Purchase Order Guide
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step1: Change Supplier - Select a different supplier if needed.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step2: Change PIC - Replace the employee responsible for this purchase order.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step3: Change PO Date and Time - Reset the order date and time.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step4: Edit Order Items - Change quantity, price, or add/remove ordered items.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step5: Total auto-recalculated - The system recalculates the total based on changes.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step6: Update Notes (optional) - Update notes for the supplier or delivery information.
guide.editPurchaseOrder.step7: Save Changes - Click Save to update the purchase order.
guide.addIngredient.title: Add Ingredient Guide
guide.addIngredient.step1: Ingredient Name (*) - Enter the name of the ingredient or raw material.
guide.addIngredient.step2: Source, Category & Supplier - Choose "No supplier" for ingredients bought at the market or made in-house, or "From a supplier" to pick a supplier and take the name, price and unit from its catalog. Then set the category.
guide.addIngredient.step3: Unit Conversion - Set purchase unit, base unit (smallest unit), and conversion factor (e.g. 1 kg = 1000 gram).
guide.addIngredient.step4: Stock & Min Stock - Set initial stock quantity and minimum stock threshold for low stock alerts.
guide.addIngredient.step5: Cost Price - Enter the purchase cost price per unit.
guide.addIngredient.step6: Status (Active/Inactive) - Active ingredients appear in purchase order item search.
guide.addIngredient.step7: Save - Click Save to create the ingredient. It will be available in PO item search.
guide.stock.s27adesc: Perform stock opname to reconcile physical stock with system records. Upload Excel or fill manually, then save to update inventory.
guide.stock.s27bdesc: View all stock changes: new products, sales, purchases, adjustments, and transfers between stores.
guide.stock.s27cdesc: Monitor products with stock below minimum threshold. Use this to plan reorders and prevent stockouts.

guide.addBom.title: BOM Writing Guide
guide.addBom.intro: A BOM (Bill of Materials) defines the raw materials and quantities needed to produce one product. Follow these steps so material requirements are calculated correctly.
guide.addBom.step1: Select the store that owns the recipe. The BOM only applies to products in that store.
guide.addBom.step2: Choose the finished product to produce. If available, set a version or recipe label so it is easy to identify.
guide.addBom.step3: Add each raw material, enter the quantity per production run, and choose its unit. Quantity must be greater than 0.
guide.addBom.step4: Supplier is optional. Use the line note for details such as 'after peeling', and the global note for instructions that apply to the whole recipe.
guide.addBom.step5: Review total material requirements, then click Save or Save as Draft. Cancel discards unsaved changes.
guide.addBom.tip1: At least one material with a quantity greater than 0 is required.
guide.addBom.tip2: Save as Draft if the recipe is not final; drafts are not used for production calculations.
guide.addBundle.title: Bundle Creation Guide
guide.addBundle.intro: A bundle sells several products as one package at a special price. Make sure the products, quantities, validity period, and package price are correct.
guide.addBundle.step1: Select the store where the bundle is sold.
guide.addBundle.step2: Enter a clear bundle name and a short description of what it includes.
guide.addBundle.step3: Set start and end dates if the bundle is only available for a limited period.
guide.addBundle.step4: Add the bundle products and enter each quantity. At least one product must have a quantity greater than 0.
guide.addBundle.step5: Upload an optional image so the bundle is easy to recognize in product lists.
guide.addBundle.step6: Enter the bundle price, review the summary, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addBundle.tip1: The bundle price should be lower than the total normal price to be attractive.
guide.addBundle.tip2: A bundle with an end date is not active outside that period.
guide.addBusinessTrip.title: Business Trip Request Guide
guide.addBusinessTrip.intro: A business trip records the destination, participants, and budget plan (RAB). Complete the details so the request can be approved and executed.
guide.addBusinessTrip.step1: Select the origin store for the trip.
guide.addBusinessTrip.step2: Enter the destination, trip purpose, departure date, return date, and any notes.
guide.addBusinessTrip.step3: Add the employees joining the trip. At least one employee is required.
guide.addBusinessTrip.step4: Build the budget items such as transport, accommodation, and per diem with quantity, unit, and rate.
guide.addBusinessTrip.step5: Review the total budget, then Save as Draft or submit it through the approval flow.
guide.addBusinessTrip.tip1: The return date cannot be earlier than the departure date.
guide.addBusinessTrip.tip2: The budget can be completed in stages, but the total must be correct before final submission.
guide.addDriver.title: Driver Setup Guide
guide.addDriver.intro: Driver data is used when assigning deliveries. Complete the identity, contact, and vehicle details so the driver can be selected in the delivery module.
guide.addDriver.step1: Enter the driver's full name as shown on their ID.
guide.addDriver.step2: Add an active phone number and email so delivery coordination runs smoothly.
guide.addDriver.step3: Select the vehicle type and enter the usual license plate number.
guide.addDriver.step4: Set the driver status. Inactive drivers cannot be assigned to new deliveries.
guide.addDriver.step5: Add notes if needed, then click Save.
guide.addDriver.tip1: Use a unique phone number so drivers are not confused with each other.
guide.addDriver.tip2: Update the vehicle details when the driver changes vehicles.
guide.addDiscount.title: Discount Creation Guide
guide.addDiscount.intro: Discounts support percentage, nominal, buy X get Y, and bundle pricing. The fields shown depend on the selected discount type.
guide.addDiscount.step1: Select the store where the discount applies.
guide.addDiscount.step2: Enter the discount name and choose the appropriate promo type.
guide.addDiscount.step3: Choose the discount type and value, such as percentage, nominal, buy/get quantity, or bundle price.
guide.addDiscount.step4: Set the target products, discount percentage, active hours, and active days as needed.
guide.addDiscount.step5: Review the summary, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addDiscount.tip1: The discount only applies to the selected products, categories, or schedule.
guide.addDiscount.tip2: Make sure the discount does not exceed the selling price so the transaction total never goes negative.
guide.addExpenseCategory.title: Expense Category Setup Guide
guide.addExpenseCategory.intro: Expense categories keep cost reports organized. Each category can be linked to an accounting account code.
guide.addExpenseCategory.step1: Enter a short, recognizable category name.
guide.addExpenseCategory.step2: Add a description explaining the costs that belong to this category.
guide.addExpenseCategory.step3: Enter the account code from the chart of accounts if accounting integration is used.
guide.addExpenseCategory.step4: Activate the category so it appears when creating a new expense.
guide.addExpenseCategory.step5: Click Save or Save as Draft once the data is correct.
guide.addExpenseCategory.tip1: Use a unique account code to avoid posting mistakes.
guide.addExpenseCategory.tip2: Inactive categories remain in history but do not appear for new transactions.
guide.addExpense.title: Expense Recording Guide
guide.addExpense.intro: Expenses can be recorded once or on a recurring basis. Fill in the store, category, amount, and payment method so cash and expense reports stay accurate.
guide.addExpense.step1: Select the store and expense date.
guide.addExpense.step2: Choose a category, enter a description, and set the expense amount.
guide.addExpense.step3: Select the payment method, payee, and frequency if the expense recurs.
guide.addExpense.step4: For recurring expenses, set an end date so the schedule does not run indefinitely.
guide.addExpense.step5: Add notes or an attachment if needed.
guide.addExpense.step6: Review the summary, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addExpense.tip1: The amount must be greater than 0 and cannot exceed available cash.
guide.addExpense.tip2: A draft does not affect cash or reports until it is saved as final.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.title: Goods Receipt Guide
guide.addGoodsReceipt.intro: A goods receipt records incoming items against a purchase order. Once saved as final, stock increases and the PO status is updated.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.step1: Select the store and the purchase order to receive. Only open POs can be selected.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.step2: Enter the received date, PIC name, delivery note number, and tax invoice number if available.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.step3: Check the PO items and enter the received quantity based on the goods that actually arrived.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.step4: Use barcode scan or enter batch, expiry date, and item condition manually.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.step5: Add notes, then Save as Draft or Save as final.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.tip1: The received quantity cannot exceed the remaining PO quantity.
guide.addGoodsReceipt.tip2: Saving as final increases stock; a draft does not change stock yet.
guide.addGoodsRequest.title: Goods Request Guide
guide.addGoodsRequest.intro: A goods request is sent to suppliers based on store needs. Requests can be grouped by supplier for easier processing.
guide.addGoodsRequest.step1: Select the store, enter the requester name, request date, and needed date.
guide.addGoodsRequest.step2: Add the supplier groups to send the request to.
guide.addGoodsRequest.step3: Enter the requested items with quantity, unit, and a note per line.
guide.addGoodsRequest.step4: Review the requirements and the needed date.
guide.addGoodsRequest.step5: Add notes, then Save as Draft or submit the request.
guide.addGoodsRequest.tip1: At least one supplier and one item are required.
guide.addGoodsRequest.tip2: The needed date should be after the request date.
guide.addProductionOrder.title: Production Order Guide
guide.addProductionOrder.intro: A production order calculates material needs from the product BOM and schedules production. Make sure the product and quantity are correct.
guide.addProductionOrder.step1: Select the finished product to produce.
guide.addProductionOrder.step2: Enter the production quantity. Quantity must be greater than 0.
guide.addProductionOrder.step4: Add notes for any special production instructions.
guide.addProductionOrder.step5: Review material requirements, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addProductionOrder.tip1: The product BOM must be complete so material needs can be calculated.
guide.addProductionOrder.tip2: A draft does not consume material stock or add finished product stock.
guide.addPromo.title: Promo Campaign Guide
guide.addPromo.intro: A promo campaign defines discount rules, bonuses, and usage limits. Set the campaign type, period, and targets correctly.
guide.addPromo.step1: Select the store, then enter the name, description, and promo code if needed.
guide.addPromo.step2: Choose the campaign type and discount type.
guide.addPromo.step3: Enter the discount value, price, or reward configuration for the selected type.
guide.addPromo.step4: Set the campaign start and end dates.
guide.addPromo.step5: Add product, tier, and reward rules plus usage limits if applicable.
guide.addPromo.step6: Review the summary, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addPromo.tip1: The promo code must be unique per store.
guide.addPromo.tip2: Bonus and reward rules must reference products that are still active.
guide.addReservation.title: Reservation Guide
guide.addReservation.intro: A reservation records a customer's planned visit, including time, guest count, and table. This helps the team prepare the space.
guide.addReservation.step1: Select the store where the reservation is made.
guide.addReservation.step3: Enter the start and end time. The end time must be after the start time.
guide.addReservation.step4: Enter the customer name, phone, email, guest count, and table if already assigned.
guide.addReservation.step5: Add special notes, then click Save.
guide.addReservation.tip1: The table is optional and can be assigned when the customer arrives.
guide.addReservation.tip2: A phone number helps the team confirm any schedule changes.
guide.createSalesReturn.title: Sales Return Guide
guide.createSalesReturn.intro: A sales return sends back some or all items from a paid order. Stock and refunds are processed after the return is saved.
guide.createSalesReturn.step1: Select a paid order to return.
guide.createSalesReturn.step2: Choose the items to return and adjust the return quantity. Quantity cannot exceed the sold quantity.
guide.createSalesReturn.step3: Select the most appropriate return reason.
guide.createSalesReturn.step4: Choose the refund method and make sure it matches the customer's original payment.
guide.createSalesReturn.step5: Add notes, review the refund total, then confirm the return.
guide.createSalesReturn.tip1: Only paid orders can be returned.
guide.createSalesReturn.tip2: A saved return restores stock and records the refund.
guide.addShiftTemplate.title: Shift Template Guide
guide.addShiftTemplate.intro: A shift template stores a reusable working-hours pattern for employee schedules.
guide.addShiftTemplate.step1: Enter a template name, such as Morning Shift or Night Shift.
guide.addShiftTemplate.step2: Set the shift start and end times.
guide.addShiftTemplate.step3: Add a description if there are special rules.
guide.addShiftTemplate.step4: Activate the template so it can be selected when building schedules.
guide.addShiftTemplate.step5: Click Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addShiftTemplate.tip1: The end time must be after the start time; overnight shifts are configured separately when supported.
guide.addShiftTemplate.tip2: Inactive templates do not appear when building new schedules.
guide.addStockTransfer.title: Stock Transfer Guide
guide.addStockTransfer.intro: A stock transfer moves items between stores. Source stock decreases when shipped and destination stock increases after receipt.
guide.addStockTransfer.step1: Select the source and destination stores. They must be different.
guide.addStockTransfer.step2: Enter the sender name, transfer reason, and expected arrival date.
guide.addStockTransfer.step3: Add items, quantity, unit, and a note per line. Quantity cannot exceed available stock.
guide.addStockTransfer.step5: Review the summary, then click Send Transfer.
guide.addStockTransfer.tip1: A transfer cannot be sent if the source stock is insufficient.
guide.addStockTransfer.tip2: The transfer status changes to received after the destination store confirms it.
guide.addUser.title: User Setup Guide
guide.addUser.intro: A new user can sign in according to the assigned role and location. Make sure the email and role are correct.
guide.addUser.step1: Enter the user's full name and active email address.
guide.addUser.step2: Set an initial password that meets the security policy.
guide.addUser.step3: Enter a phone number for verification and coordination.
guide.addUser.step4: Select the location/store and role that match the user's responsibilities.
guide.addUser.step5: Review the data, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addUser.tip1: The email must be unique; an already registered email cannot be used again.
guide.addUser.tip2: The role determines menus and permissions; choose the role with the least access needed.
guide.addRole.title: Role Creation Guide
guide.addRole.intro: A role defines the set of permissions granted to users. Create roles that match responsibilities so access stays controlled.
guide.addRole.step1: Enter a unique, easy-to-understand role name.
guide.addRole.step2: Add a description of the role's responsibilities.
guide.addRole.step3: Choose the role type if available.
guide.addRole.step4: Check the required permissions in the permission matrix.
guide.addRole.step5: Review the summary, then Save or Save as Draft.
guide.addRole.tip1: Avoid granting full administrator permissions when they are not needed.
guide.addRole.tip2: A new role can be selected immediately when adding or editing a user.
guide.editRole.title: Role Editing Guide
guide.editRole.intro: Changes to a role immediately affect every user assigned to it. Review permissions carefully before saving.
guide.editRole.step1: Review the role name and description, and update them if needed.
guide.editRole.step2: Adjust permissions in the permission matrix.
guide.editRole.step3: Read the change summary to ensure no access was removed unintentionally.
guide.editRole.step4: Click Save to apply the changes.
guide.editRole.tip1: Permission changes apply to every user with this role.
guide.editRole.tip2: Make sure at least one user still has administrator access.
guide.editCategory.title: Product Category Editing Guide
guide.editCategory.intro: Categories group products. Changes to the name, parent, color, icon, and status appear in product lists.
guide.editCategory.step1: Select the store that owns the category.
guide.editCategory.step2: Update the category name and description if needed.
guide.editCategory.step3: Choose a parent category to build a hierarchy, or leave it empty for a top-level category.
guide.editCategory.step4: Set the color and sort order so categories are easy to distinguish.
guide.editCategory.step5: Choose an icon and activate the category so it appears in product selection.
guide.editCategory.step6: Click Save or Save as Draft.
guide.editCategory.tip1: A category cannot be its own parent.
guide.editCategory.tip2: Deactivating a category does not delete products that already use it.
guide.editIngredientCategory.title: Ingredient Category Editing Guide
guide.editIngredientCategory.intro: Ingredient categories group raw materials in inventory. Name and status changes appear immediately in ingredient lists.
guide.editIngredientCategory.step1: Update the category name if needed. Use a unique, searchable name.
guide.editIngredientCategory.step2: Set the active status. Inactive categories do not appear when adding new raw materials.
guide.editIngredientCategory.step3: Click Save or Save as Draft.
guide.editIngredientCategory.tip1: The category name must be unique so it is not confusing to select.
guide.editIngredientCategory.tip2: Deactivating a category does not delete raw materials that are already linked to it.
